title: Norway Maple: Ancient Norway Maples You Can Visit
meta_description: One of Europe's most-planted, most-replaceable street trees. Three survive: a Den Bosch fortress bastion, two Munich squares an ordinance protects.
intro: Norway maple is one of the most planted street trees in Europe, valued for tolerating road salt, compacted soil and bad air, and just as routinely cut back once it outgrows its spot. The three mapped here are what a city decided to keep instead. One stands on a two-metre-thick fortress bastion in Den Bosch, on parkland made after the earthwork's old defensive windmill came down and the ramparts stopped being military. Munich protects two more under a 2021 natural monument ordinance built for the exception rather than the rule: one on Mondstrasse is named a singular tree that defines its square, the other on Herrnstrasse survives simply for being rare at its size among five storeys of inner-city courtyards. Snap a leaf stalk on either and it bleeds white sap, the surest way to tell a Norway maple from the sycamore maple it is otherwise mistaken for.
